/**
 * nsMsgKey is a unique ID for a particular message in a folder. If you want a
 * handle to a message that will remain valid even after resorting the folder or
 * otherwise changing their indices, you want one of these rather than a
 * nsMsgViewIndex. nsMsgKeys don't survive local mail folder compression,
 * however.
 *
 * In cases where the message key is not available yet (e.g. a header waiting to
 * be persisted), `0xffffffff` is used as a placeholder.
 */
typedef unsigned long nsMsgKey;

/**
 * nsMsgViewIndex is generic index type from which other index types are
 * derived. All nsMsgViewIndex derived types are zero based.
 *
 * The following index types are currently supported:
 *  - nsMsgViewIndex - an index into the list of messages or folders or groups,
 *    where zero is the first one to show, one is the second, etc...
 *  - AB_SelectionIndex
 *  - AB_NameCompletionIndex
 *
 * In cases where this index is not available yet (e.g. a header waiting to be
 * persisted), `0xffffffff` is used as a placeholder.
 */
typedef unsigned long nsMsgViewIndex;

const nsMsgKey nsMsgKey_None = 0xffffffff;
const nsMsgViewIndex nsMsgViewIndex_None = 0xFFFFFFFF;

// Map of all the messages we want to keep. storeToken => messageKey
  mozilla::HashMap<nsCString, nsMsgKey> mMsgsToKeep;

source.basis: Quoted evidence supports the claim; its interpretation still needs current-source checks.

text: MailNewsTypes2 distinguishes a message key from the zero-based view index that can change when the view is reordered, and documents 0xffffffff as a missing-value placeholder. Current FolderCompactor preserves the database key while updating its store token. Therefore do not teach the old copied sentence that keys universally fail to survive folder compression; scope lifetime claims to the current store/database implementation. Keep key, view index and store token names distinct at API boundaries. This is static source evidence. No runtime, build or accessibility session was run. Full bug and review discussion remains pending.
title: Distinguish stable message keys from view indices and storage tokens
